The fin fan cooler hood was not recognized as a Confined Space with Special Hazardous Characteristics. CSEP was not submitted and CSE-specific hazards and safeguards were not identified in the JSA.

No documented CSE-specific rescue plan or rescue arrangement was established for two workers inside the hood/above the fan blade. EEBA was available for emergency escape but does not replace rescue preparedness for an incapacitated entrant.

The PA remained outside the hood and maintained oversight; however, the activity was not recognized as CSE and an emergency egress response was not established. In the event of a PGD alarm, the mobile staircase had to be repositioned to the hood access point, creating potential delay in evacuating the two entrants.

Fall Restraint vs Fall Arrest Selection

Workers used a fall arrest system; however, they were unable to explain how to determine when fall restraint should be selected instead of fall arrest. The system selection appeared to be based on the fall arrest equipment being available rather than a hierarchy-based assessment of preventing access to the fall hazard first.
Fall Arrest vs Fall Restraint Lanyard
Workers were unable to clearly explain the technical difference between fall restraint, which prevents reaching the fall hazard, and fall arrest, which stops a worker after a fall has occurred.

No fall clearance calculation was demonstrated for the approximately 2.5 m working height. The effectiveness of the fall arrest system to arrest the worker before contact with the lower surface/fan structure was not verified..
The selected anchorage point was not verified to meet the required 5,000 lbf / 22.2 kN capacity or an engineered anchorage system with a safety factor of 2.
The anchorage position and potential fall path were not demonstrated to prevent contact with the fan blade, structure or lower surface during a fall.
No documented fall rescue plan was available despite the use of a personal fall arrest system. No specific arrangement for prompt rescue and suspension trauma response was demonstrated.

Initial gas testing prior to hot work was not observed during the document review; therefore, verification of gas monitoring at potential LEL sources and within the 15-metre buffer zone could not be performed.

The JSA requires gas testing to confirm no flammable gas before the 24 VDC voltage check and specifies spark prevention. However, the reviewed JSA does not identify the hazardous area classification of the work location or document how the area classification is used to determine ignition-source controls for the voltage-checking activity.
